Tal.et: Inherited from Middle High German tal, from Old High German tal. Cognate with Danish dal, Dutch dal, English dale, Swedish dal.

Taler.et: Clipping of Joachimstaler, the name of a coin first minted in Joachimsthal, Bohemia around 1518, soon after the discovery of silver deposits there. Ultimately from Joachim + Thal (“valley”), now spelled Tal. Cognate to Low German Daler. Doublet of Dollar

Talk.et: Borrowed from English talk, in part by clipping from Talkshow, from English talk show.

s: Taliban, a member of the Taliban movement

Taliban.et: From Pashto طالبان (tālibān), plural of طالب (tālib, “disciple”).

Talg.et: Borrowed from Middle Low German talch, from Old Saxon *talg, from Proto-West Germanic *talg, from Proto-Germanic *talgaz. More at tallow.

s: Taliban (member of the Taliban movement or its militia)

talentvoll.et: From Talent + -voll. Compare Saterland Frisian talentful.

s: vale of tears (a place or state of sorrow)
Tal der Tränen.et: Calque of Latin lacrimārum vallis in the Salve Regina, referring there to the world as a whole. Thence also English vale of tears.

Talkmaster.et: Talk(show) + English master, modelled after Showmaster.
